page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio (8.0 GB per core). The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96s_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, achieving top 10% placement in both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only tests. Multi-core processing capabilities are strong, with stress-ng multi-core performance in the top 25% and Passmark CPU scores in the top 10%. The hardware excels in data processing tasks, showing top-tier results in gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Passmark database operations. Redis SET operations reach 160.72 million operations per second, placing it in the top 10%. For AI workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference shows top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds fall into the average to strong categories.

The instance offers high resource density and memory capacity, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound enterprise workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. However, the lack of bundled local storage means users must rely on external Premium Storage, which introduces external network dependency for I/O operations. Single-core CPU performance is average, indicating that workloads relying on single-threaded execution may not fully leverage the hardware's premium profile. The E96s_v7 is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and CPU-based machine learning inference tasks.
